wins.need: Recharging fast from a wall outlet between outages
wins.claim: Measured going from empty to full on 110 V in about an hour, pulling slightly more than its rated 1,500 W input. None of the sources I read measured a rival's charge time, so this is a measured figure, not a measured win over a named rival.
wins.figure: 0-50% in 33 min, 0-80% in 53 min, 0-100% in 1 h 7 min; peak AC input measured at about 1,538 W at 110 V

wins.need: Adding capacity later for less money
wins.claim: VTOMAN's 1,548 Wh add-on battery, sold for the FlashSpeed 1500, costs less per Wh than a whole 1.5-2 kWh station from Jackery or BLUETTI (arithmetic; this compares an add-on battery with complete stations)
wins.figure: Arithmetic: $379.99 / 1,548 Wh = $0.25/Wh for the add-on battery, against Jackery Explorer 1500 v2 at $849 / 1,536 Wh = $0.55/Wh and BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 at $899 / 2,080 Wh = $0.43/Wh. Total with the add-on is 3,096 Wh.
wins.who: Arithmetic on maker store prices (VTOMAN, Jackery, BLUETTI)

wins.need: Running a full 1,500 W load (kettle, coffee maker, space heater) without cutting out
wins.claim: Held a continuous 1,500 W AC load until the battery was empty. No rival was tested the same way in the sources I read.
wins.figure: 1,500 W continuous: 50% left after 23 min, 20% after 38 min, empty at 47 min. Arithmetic: 1,500 W x 47/60 h is about 1,175 Wh, roughly 76% of the rated 1,548 Wh at full load.

weak.claim: Lower rated AC output than similarly priced rivals
weak.figure: 1,500 W rated / 3,000 W peak, against 2,000 W / 4,000 W surge for Jackery Explorer 1500 v2 (jackery.com) and 2,600 W for BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (bluettipower.com)

weak.claim: Slower UPS switchover than EcoFlow's claim. ChargerLAB says the UPS is not professional grade and not suitable for medical equipment.
weak.figure: 20 ms switchover (an iMac stayed on in ChargerLAB's single test), against EcoFlow's claimed 10 ms auto-switch on the DELTA 3 Classic

weak.claim: Jump-starting underperformed in a hands-on test
weak.figure: Off Road Xtreme (Jason Gonderman) says it cranked the starter only a handful of times before overheating and shutting down

weak.claim: Heavy, no app, confusing display, and a loud fan that runs nonstop while charging in hot weather
weak.figure: Gadgetoid: 18.8 kg; no app or connectivity; the display doesn't say whether the watts shown are in or out; fan loud and runs continuously while charging in heat

weak.claim: Real solar input fell well short of a 400 W panel's rating, through an Anderson connector that may need an adapter
weak.figure: Gadgetoid saw about 20 W in rain, 50 W on an overcast day, up to 140 W on sunnier days and 250 W in a heatwave from a 400 W panel

weak.claim: Charging at 1,500 W can trip breakers in older homes and is too much for most consumer gas generators; the add-on battery can only be charged through the main unit

wins_for: Someone who wants about 1.5 kWh of LFP storage now and may double it to 3,096 Wh later with VTOMAN's $379.99 add-on battery (maker store, 2026-11-15)
Someone who needs a full recharge from a 120 V outlet in about an hour between outages (ChargerLAB measured 1 h 7 min)
Backup for a desktop computer or router where a 20 ms switchover is acceptable (ChargerLAB's iMac test)
not_for: Appliances above 1,500 W: Jackery Explorer 1500 v2 (2,000 W) or BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (2,600 W) win instead
Medical equipment or loads that need a fast UPS switch: ChargerLAB rules out medical use. EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic claims 10 ms.
Jump-starting a vehicle: Off Road Xtreme's unit overheated after a few cranks
Carrying any distance: 18.8 kg per Gadgetoid and the maker manual
Shoppers who want app monitoring: Gadgetoid found none. EcoFlow's DELTA 3 Ultra Plus store listing describes app control.

rivals.where_it_beats_ours: 2,000 W AC / 4,000 W surge against 1,500 W / 3,000 W (Jackery store text)
2,600 W output and 2,080 Wh capacity, per the listing title
Claims a 10 ms auto-switch (against 20 ms) and 1,800 W output, but has about 524 Wh less capacity
Listed as 1,800 W AC (3,600 W surge) against 1,500 W, and confirmed buyable on Amazon today
1,800 W constant / 3,600 W peak per the store text. It is VTOMAN's own model and was listed in the store today.

targets.headline: Which VTOMAN power station is worth buying?
targets.why_it_wins_there: Within VTOMAN's range it is a 1,500 W unit that ChargerLAB measured charging from empty to full in 1 h 7 min, and VTOMAN sells a 1,548 Wh add-on battery for it at $379.99 (vtoman.com, 2026-11-15). Hold this page until the base unit's price and an Amazon listing are confirmed, because today's store search showed no standalone FlashSpeed 1500 listing.

targets.headline: VTOMAN power stations compared: fast charging, add-on batteries and real output
targets.why_it_wins_there: Same as above: measured hour-long recharge (ChargerLAB) and a cheap way to add capacity (arithmetic: $0.25/Wh for the add-on battery). I found no measured reason it wins any generic search with volume against Jackery, BLUETTI or EcoFlow, and its 1,500 W rating loses on output to rivals at $849-899.

record.name: VTOMAN FlashSpeed 1500 Portable Power Station (1,548 Wh, 1,500 W)
specs: 1,548 Wh (3,096 Wh with the extra battery)
1,500 W rated, 3,000 W peak, pure sine wave, 3 outlets
record.warranty: 24 months from purchase for the original buyer, battery cells excluded, per the PB-58 manual (230 V edition) at https://www.manualslib.com/manual/3390316/Vtoman-Pb-58.html, read 2026-11-15
record.returns: Not confirmed: there is no Amazon listing to take terms from, and VTOMAN's site returned HTTP 429
record.summary: A 1,548 Wh LiFePO4 power station with 1,500 W output that ChargerLAB measured recharging from a wall outlet in 1 h 7 min, and which takes a 1,548 Wh add-on battery.
record.fit: Home-outage backup and car camping for someone who wants a fast wall recharge and the option to double capacity later, and who doesn't need more than 1,500 W.
caveats: Rated at 1,500 W, below Jackery Explorer 1500 v2 (2,000 W) and BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (2,600 W) (maker stores, 2026-11-15)
20 ms UPS switchover; ChargerLAB says it is not for medical equipment
Jump-start overheated after a few cranks (Off Road Xtreme)
18.8 kg, no app, loud fan when charging in heat (Gadgetoid)
Off Road Xtreme's Jason Gonderman says the marketing calls the inverter pure sine wave but the owner's manual differs

unsourced: Amazon ASIN, title and seller: I could not confirm a listing from VTOMAN or Amazon, so asin is null. amzcheck search returned nothing for three queries. B0G4CPF8NQ and B0CNCZSRQV (the search snippets title them FlashSpeed 1500) came back 'blocked' from amzcheck four times and HTTP 503 from WebFetch. B0C8T2C8DB, which manuals.plus ties to the FlashSpeed 1500, now opens on Amazon as 'VTOMAN FlashSpeed 300 Portable Power Station, 300W 230Wh LiFePO4 Battery' (read 2026-11-15).

That may mean it is discontinued, but I could not confirm it.
